In simple words, explain LoRA.

{"answer": "A PEFT method that freezes pretrained weights, represents weight updates as a low-rank product of two small matrices, and trains only those small matrices. It trains few parameters and saves the results (adapters) in small files. The Lecture 02 exercises cover LoRA.", "needs_review": false}

In simple words, explain QLoRA.

{"answer": "A method that saves memory by quantizing base-model weights to, for example, 4 bits, then trains with LoRA. This lets smaller GPUs handle larger models. In the Lecture 02 exercises, the model fits in GPU memory, so we train with LoRA and compare memory and output differences when loading in 4-bit in the advanced section.", "needs_review": false}

In simple words, explain Token.

{"answer": "The smallest unit an LLM uses to process text. Text is split into fragments of words or characters. API charges, rate limits, and context window sizes are often counted in tokens. Tokenization varies by language; for example, Japanese tends to require more tokens per character than English.", "needs_review": false}
